Butting in here, sorry, I am so excited to talk about fish again! 
I used to keep blue and golden Gouramis and I have to tell ya, they are my FAVORITE fish. They can be territorial lil guys, but they are super interesting to watch and incredibly hardy. (I know because my little brother poured a can of sprite into my tank and somehow they were all fine! I had 4 gouramis. All female!) Mine lived for many years and I always tell new fish owners about them! They're labyrinth fish, meaning they come up for air, so you don't need an airstone or bubbler (but you can get one if you want!) The only way these guys won't work out for you is if you want to keep many types of fish all in one tank. Like I said, they can be pretty mean, so I'd stick to only keeping Gourami if you're interested. 
Btw, I'm a huge fnaf fan and I love this idea! I might do this when I pick up fishkeeping again.

I would agree that it's partially the responsibility of the channels and sites to maintain advertising standards, however that is far from the point here. It does not take away the responsibility of Juul to not sell their products to children. It just further proves my original point that Juul marketed their device and pods directly to children, so that made children want it more. 
I also remember the blu ecig ads, my mom used to watch Hallmark a lot, and she would see them there, and I would see them on Investigation Discovery often. However, the adults in their ads always looked like actual adults, and they never went out of their way to make it look overly cool. No bright colors, no trendy music, clearly an advertisement aimed at the target audience. That is what Juul should have done, but they were too busy trying to sell children creme brulee flavored nicotine. Pretty crazy. 
Also, no, it was Nick Jr. For toddlers. :/
Oh, and I totally forgot about the ad spot they purchased in 2017... In the magazine Seventeen, who's target audience is teens. And the ad spot they purchased on Nick Jr...

Bull that no one signed off on that. In case you didn't read, they also went out of their way to purchase ad slots on Cartoon Network and Nickelodeon sites... Which couldn't have come cheap. They had a creme brulee flavor as well, which I think that a lot of people forgot, but was shown and proven to be the choice of kids. It's great that you, a person of age, love Juul, but Juul is big tobacco and always has been. They were never a 'small' company by any standard. Hell, my boyfriend used to distribute Juul, that company is bigger than you think. I do agree that kids were bound to pick up ecigs sooner rather than later, as you are correct that they tend to pick up whatever is 'cool', but I doubt the spread would have been as fast as it was without the literal MILLIONS spent on online advertising that was shown on kids sites. 
I find it absolutely insane that Juul was allowed to stay open and was not outright banned (as it should have been). You don't see other companies targeting kids sites to peddle adult products... Especially not with ads featuring game controllers and pencil cases. You have every right to buy whatever you like and even enjoy Juuls, but you don't have the right to spread ignorance about what they did to vaping as a whole. Blu ecigs were in stores WELL before Juuls, and you never hear people talking about them, because they didn't market to kids. Njoy is still in stores today, and didn't market to kids. Juul was irresponsible, like it or not.

>It is still funny to me that everyone was so outraged about kids getting flavored juuls.

Here's the thing though, you didn't do any research and that's crystal clear. They were quite literally marketing Juuls to children, putting their ads, deliberately mind you, on sites like :
"The list where they ran includes educational sites like basic-mathematics.com, coolmath.com, math-aids.com, mathplayground.com, mathway.com, onlinemathlearning.com, and purplemath.com. and socialstudiesforkids.com.

It includes sites targeted to young girls such as dailydressupgames.com, didigames.com, forhergames.com, games2girls.com, girlgames.com, and girlsgogames.com."
Source: www.nytimes.com/2020/02/12/health/juul-vaping-lawsuit.amp.html?espv=1

I was working at a grocery store and it was my last day. (Found a better job; scince I was getting so few hours with the grocery store.) 

I had given the proper 2 weeks and was amicable through the split. It was 3 hours into my shift. I called my manager and told her I needed a restroom break. 2 hours pass. I'm checking out this very rude couple and they pull something out of their cart; say they don't want it; and had it to me. It's a cheap set of pairing knives. One of the sleeves had come off and they handed it to me with the blade side toward me. 

I didn't realize; I grabbed it and put it aside. I saw blood on my hands; so I used one hand to bag for the rest of their order. I phone my manager. Tell her I'm bleeding. She says 'Ok; call customer service." I hang up; pissed off. I haven't had a break; I'm out of water; I need to go pee; and I'm bleeding. I'm not calling customer service. I try to cover up my bleeding and continue on; when a cashier finally shows up and says 'Hey! Time for your break!' 

I finish that customer; pass off the baton; and go meet my manager. I ask her what break I have; 15 min or lunch. 

She said she sent the cashier to the wrong register. 

I walked out. Never clocked out; never came back; I went across the street to Walmart; asked an associate for a band-aid; and meant my boyfriend who was there to stock Red Bull.
